def _tally_pac_fork_rows(
    rows: list[dict],
) -> tuple[bool, dict[str, _PAFD_EDGE_SET]]:
    """Group authenticated rows per site by their complete edge sets.

    Two rows from one site are the same declaration only when their
    complete fork edge set -- every ``(rootDigest, predecessorDigest,
    successors)`` triple -- agrees, regardless of the proof digest.
    The smallest-id row of one identical set is the vote and extras are
    ``duplicate``, while two distinct edge sets from one site are both a
    ``contradiction``.  Returns ``(contradicted, votes)`` where
    ``votes`` maps each non-contradicting site to its one edge set.
    """
    by_site: dict[str, dict[_PAFD_EDGE_SET, list[dict]]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        if row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] in (
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION,
        ):
            by_site.setdefault(row[VD_ISSUER], {}).setdefault(
                _pafd_content(row), []
            ).append(row)

    contradicted = False
    votes: dict[str, _PAFD_EDGE_SET] = {}
    for site, groups in by_site.items():
        if len(groups) > 1:
            contradicted = True
            ordered_groups = sorted(
                groups.values(),
                key=lambda members: min(member[ID] for member in members),
            )
            for members in ordered_groups:
                members.sort(key=lambda row: row[ID])
                members[0][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION
                members[0][ADJ_REASON] = REASON_CONTRADICTION
                for extra in members[1:]:
                    extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
                    extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
        else:
            content, members = next(iter(groups.items()))
            members.sort(key=lambda row: row[ID])
            members[0][ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID
            members[0][ADJ_REASON] = None
            for extra in members[1:]:
                extra[ADJ_CONCLUSION] = _PAFD_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
                extra[ADJ_REASON] = REASON_DUPLICATE
            votes[site] = content
    return contradicted, votes


def adjudicate_prune_aggregate_forks(
    items, prune_policy, site_policy, keyring, moment, issuer, version
):
    """Adjudicate multi-site prune aggregate fork proofs offline.

    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a unique
    non-empty ``id`` and ``proof`` bytes produced by
    :func:`sign_prune_aggregate_fork_proof`.  ``prune_policy`` is the
    shared invariant original ``{"batch","sites","threshold"}`` pruning
    policy the proofs were issued against; ``site_policy`` carries
    exactly ``sites`` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty site
    to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and
    ``threshold`` (a positive integer no greater than the site count).
    ``keyring`` follows the existing rules, ``moment`` is the
    non-negative adjudication moment and ``issuer``/``version`` name the
    adjudicator credentials.  No file is read or written and no input is
    modified.

    Every proof is first verified through the existing prune aggregate
    fork proof rules, then authorized by the exact signing site and key
    version its payload names with no fallback, then authenticated
    against the current keyring.  An invalid, unauthenticated or
    unauthorized proof rejects just that item with one fixed reason
    (``invalid-proof``, ``unauthorized-site``, ``unauthorized-version``,
    ``credential-unavailable``, ``revoked``, ``not-yet-valid``,
    ``expired`` or ``bad-signature``) while the later items are still
    processed.  For one site the complete fork edge set counts once --
    extra proofs declaring an identical edge set are ``duplicate`` --
    while distinct valid edge sets from one site are a
    ``contradiction``.  Distinct sites must agree exactly on the
    complete fork edge set made of the root digest, the forking
    predecessor digest and the sorted legal successor digests; any
    contradiction or cross-site disagreement is ``conflicted`` with a
    null common edge set and no majority can outvote it.  A unique edge
    set backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is
    ``accepted``; the same unique set short of the threshold stays
    ``insufficient`` but keeps that common set; with no valid vote the
    common set is null.

    The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with
    recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte,
    carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``.  The payload binds
    exactly ``common`` (the sorted common fork edge set, or null),
    ``issuer``, ``items`` (the rows stably sorted by site then id, each
    carrying ``conclusion``, its authenticated ``edges`` or null, ``id``,
    ``keyVersion``, ``proofDigest``, ``reason`` and ``site``),
    ``keyVersion``, ``prunePolicyDigest``, ``proofs`` (each proof digest
    in the original input order), ``sitePolicyDigest``, ``status`` and
    ``version`` (the integer 1).  ``signature`` is the lowercase hex
    HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under the exact
    issuer/version key.

    A parameter, container or public-field type fault raises
    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); an empty
    list, an empty or duplicate id, or an illegal prune/site policy,
    threshold, moment, issuer or version raises :class:`ValueError`;
    unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials
    raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_pac_fork_proof_items(items)
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_site_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(site_policy)
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    if isinstance(moment, bool) or not isinstance(moment, int):
        raise TypeError("moment must be an int")
    if moment < 0:
        raise ValueError("moment must be non-negative")
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise ValueError("issuer must be non-empty")
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
        raise TypeError("version must be an int")
    if version <= 0:
        raise ValueError("version must be positive")

    prune_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _verdict_policy_bytes(validated_prune_policy)
    ).hexdigest()

    proof_digests = [
        hashlib.sha256(item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF]).hexdigest()
        for item in validated_items
    ]
    rows = [
        _adjudicate_pac_fork_one(
            item, prune_policy_digest, validated_site_policy,
            validated_keyring, moment,
        )
        for item in validated_items
    ]

    contradicted, votes = _tally_pac_fork_rows(rows)

    edge_sets = set(votes.values())
    if contradicted or len(edge_sets) > 1:
        status = _PAFD_STATUS_CONFLICTED
        common = None
    elif len(edge_sets) == 1:
        common = _sorted_pac_fork_edge_objects(next(iter(edge_sets)))
        if len(votes) >= validated_site_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD]:
            status = _PAFD_STATUS_ACCEPTED
        else:
            status = _PAFD_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
    else:
        status = _PAFD_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
        common = None

    rows.sort(
        key=lambda row: (
            row[VD_ISSUER] is not None,
            row[VD_ISSUER] or "",
            row[ID],
        )
    )

    signing_entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, issuer, version, moment
    )
    payload = {
        PAFD_COMMON: common,
        VD_ISSUER: issuer,
        ITEMS: [copy.deepcopy(row) for row in rows],
        KEY_VERSION: version,
        PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST: prune_policy_digest,
        PAFD_PROOFS: proof_digests,
        PAFD_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: hashlib.sha256(
            _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_site_policy)
        ).hexdigest(),
        STATUS: status,
        VERSION: PRUNE_AGGREGATE_FORK_DECISION_VERSION,
    }
    signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(signing_entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return _prune_compact({TICKET_PAYLOAD: payload, SIGNATURE: signature})

# -- Signed cross-site handover fork proofs over decision aggregate chains -----
#
# This layer mirrors the chain fork aggregate fork-proof/decision layer
# (``cfa``) but its source batch is :func:`verify_decision_aggregate_chains`
# -- the "decision aggregate chain" layer.  The bound report therefore uses the
# decision-aggregate-chains version and fixed conflicted error
# (``"forked-decision-aggregate-chain"``); the per-chain result shape is the
# decision aggregate chain summary (rootDigest/headDigest/height/status/
# commonDigest/policyVersion).  The wire field names and the whole
# verify-then-authorize-then-authenticate pipeline follow the ``cfa`` layer;
# only the fork-report source differs.

AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_PROOF_VERSION = 1
AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_VERSION = 1

_ACF_PROOFS_VERSION = 1
_ACF_PROOFS_VERIFIED = _CF_PROOFS_VERIFIED
_ACF_PROOFS_INVALID = _CF_PROOFS_INVALID
_ACF_PROOFS_UNAUTHENTICATED = _CF_PROOFS_UNAUTHENTICATED

_ACF_AUTHZ_POLICY_DIGEST = _CFA_AUTHZ_POLICY_DIGEST

_ACF_PROOF_TOP_KEYS = frozenset((TICKET_PAYLOAD, SIGNATURE))
_ACF_PROOF_PAYLOAD_KEYS = frozenset((
    FORK_PROOF_CHAINS,
    VD_ISSUER,
    KEY_VERSION,
    CP_MOMENT,
    CF_PROOF_PRUNE_POLICY,
    FORK_PROOF_REPORT,
    CF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY,
    VERSION,
))
_ACF_DECISION_PAYLOAD_KEYS = frozenset((
    PAFD_COMMON,
    VD_ISSUER,
    ITEMS,
    KEY_VERSION,
    PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST,
    PAFD_PROOFS,
    _ACF_AUTHZ_POLICY_DIGEST,
    STATUS,
    VERSION,
))


def _acf_proof_invalid(message: str) -> InvalidChainProofError:
    return InvalidChainProofError(
        f"invalid aggregate chain fork proof: {message}"
    )


def _acf_decision_invalid(message: str) -> InvalidChainDecisionError:
    return InvalidChainDecisionError(
        f"invalid aggregate chain fork decision: {message}"
    )


def _reject_duplicate_acf_proof_keys(pairs: list[tuple]) -> dict:
    """``object_pairs_hook`` turning duplicate proof keys into an error."""
    result: dict = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise _acf_proof_invalid(f"duplicate key {key!r} in object")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def _reject_duplicate_acf_decision_keys(pairs: list[tuple]) -> dict:
    """``object_pairs_hook`` turning duplicate decision keys into an error."""
    result: dict = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(f"duplicate key {key!r} in object")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def _parse_acf_fork_proof(raw: object) -> tuple[dict, str, list[dict]]:
    """Validate aggregate chain fork proof bytes structurally.

    Returns ``(payload, signature, chains)``.  A non-bytes argument or a
    public field of the wrong type raises :class:`TypeError` (a
    :class:`bool` never poses as an int); every encoding, key-set,
    version, digest, count, ordering, reference or report-binding fault
    raises :class:`InvalidChainProofError`.  The two policy bindings, the
    moment and the signature are checked by the proof verifier.
    """
    if not isinstance(raw, bytes):
        raise TypeError("proof must be bytes")
    if not raw or raw[-1:] in (b"\n", b"\r", b" ", b"\t"):
        raise _acf_proof_invalid(
            "must end with the closing brace, no trailing byte"
        )
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid("is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        data = json.loads(
            text, object_pairs_hook=_reject_duplicate_acf_proof_keys
        )
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid("is not valid JSON") from exc

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise TypeError("proof must be a JSON object")
    if set(data.keys()) != _ACF_PROOF_TOP_KEYS:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid(
            "must contain exactly the keys 'payload' and 'signature'"
        )
    signature = data[SIGNATURE]
    if not isinstance(signature, str):
        raise TypeError("proof signature must be a str")
    if not _prune_is_digest(signature):
        raise _acf_proof_invalid(
            "signature must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
        )
    payload = data[TICKET_PAYLOAD]
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise TypeError("proof payload must be an object")
    if set(payload.keys()) != _ACF_PROOF_PAYLOAD_KEYS:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid(
            "payload must contain exactly the keys 'chains', 'issuer', "
            "'keyVersion', 'moment', 'prunePolicy', 'report', 'sitePolicy' "
            "and 'version'"
        )
    issuer = payload[VD_ISSUER]
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("payload issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise _acf_proof_invalid("payload issuer must be a non-empty str")
    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
    if isinstance(key_version, bool) or not isinstance(key_version, int):
        raise TypeError("payload keyVersion must be an int")
    if key_version <= 0:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid("payload keyVersion must be positive")
    moment = payload[CP_MOMENT]
    if isinstance(moment, bool) or not isinstance(moment, int):
        raise TypeError("payload moment must be an int")
    if moment < 0:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid("payload moment must be non-negative")
    for field in (CF_PROOF_PRUNE_POLICY, CF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY):
        digest = payload[field]
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"payload {field} must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _acf_proof_invalid(
                f"payload {field} must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )
    version = payload[VERSION]
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
        raise TypeError("payload version must be an int")
    if version != AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_PROOF_VERSION:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid("payload version must be the integer 1")
    chains = _validated_pac_fork_chains(
        payload[FORK_PROOF_CHAINS], invalid=_acf_proof_invalid
    )
    _validated_pac_fork_report(
        payload[FORK_PROOF_REPORT], chains,
        conflicted_error=_CDA_CHAIN_ITEM_ERROR,
        invalid=_acf_proof_invalid,
        report_version=DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAINS_VERSION,
    )

    if _prune_compact(data) != raw:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid(
            "encoding is not the canonical compact form"
        )
    return payload, signature, chains


def sign_aggregate_chain_fork_proof(items, prune_policy, authorization_policy,
                                    keyring, moment, issuer, version):
    """Sign the fork summary of a decision aggregate chain batch.

    ``items`` is the same non-empty list of ``{"id", "root",
    "successors", "policies"}`` dicts
    :func:`verify_decision_aggregate_chains` takes; ``prune_policy`` is
    the shared invariant original ``{"batch","sites","threshold"}``
    pruning policy and ``authorization_policy`` the shared site
    authorization policy, ``keyring`` follows the existing rules,
    ``moment`` is the signing time and ``issuer``/``version`` name the
    signing credentials.  The batch first runs through the exact
    :func:`verify_decision_aggregate_chains` rules and the proof is
    issued only when the resulting report records at least one fork (a
    fork-free report raises :class:`ValueError`).  No file is read or
    written and no argument is modified.

    The proof is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object -- every object
    key recursively sorted, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline or
    any other trailing byte -- carrying exactly ``payload`` and
    ``signature``.  The payload binds exactly ``chains`` (every input
    chain in input order: ``id``, the ``root`` digest, every
    ``successors`` digest and the canonical digest of every versioned
    decision site policy in the complete ``policies`` history),
    ``issuer``, ``keyVersion``, ``moment``, ``prunePolicy`` (the
    lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical compact prune policy
    encoding), ``report`` (the complete chain-batch report),
    ``sitePolicy`` (the SHA-256 of the canonical compact site
    authorization policy) and ``version`` (the integer 1).  The HMAC is
    computed by the exact issuer/version identity with no fallback.

    A parameter or public field type fault raises :class:`TypeError`
    (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); an empty list, an empty or
    duplicate id, a wrong policy count, an empty issuer, a non-positive
    version, a negative moment, an illegal shared policy or a report
    without a fork raises :class:`ValueError`; and unknown, revoked,
    not-yet-valid or expired credentials raise
    :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_fac_chain_batch(items)
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_authorization_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        authorization_policy
    )
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    sign_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise ValueError("issuer must be non-empty")
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
        raise TypeError("version must be an int")
    if version <= 0:
        raise ValueError("version must be positive")

    report = verify_decision_aggregate_chains(
        validated_items, prune_policy, authorization_policy, keyring,
        sign_moment,
    )
    if not report[CHAINS_FORKS]:
        raise ValueError(
            "an aggregate chain fork proof requires at least one fork in "
            "the chain report"
        )
    entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, issuer, version, sign_moment
    )
    payload = {
        FORK_PROOF_CHAINS: _pac_chain_materials(validated_items),
        VD_ISSUER: issuer,
        KEY_VERSION: version,
        CP_MOMENT: sign_moment,
        CF_PROOF_PRUNE_POLICY: hashlib.sha256(
            _verdict_policy_bytes(validated_prune_policy)
        ).hexdigest(),
        FORK_PROOF_REPORT: copy.deepcopy(report),
        CF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY: hashlib.sha256(
            _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_authorization_policy)
        ).hexdigest(),
        VERSION: AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_PROOF_VERSION,
    }
    signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return _prune_compact({TICKET_PAYLOAD: payload, SIGNATURE: signature})


def _verify_acf_fork_proof_core(
    raw: bytes,
    validated_prune_policy: dict,
    validated_authorization_policy: dict,
    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    verify_moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify one aggregate chain fork proof against validated materials.

    Shared core of the batch verifier; the caller owns the
    argument-type and shared-material validation.  The returned dict is
    freshly built solely from authenticated proof material.
    """
    payload, signature, chains = _parse_acf_fork_proof(raw)
    expected_prune_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _verdict_policy_bytes(validated_prune_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    if payload[CF_PROOF_PRUNE_POLICY] != expected_prune_digest:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid(
            "prune policy digest does not match the prune policy"
        )
    expected_site_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_authorization_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    if payload[CF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY] != expected_site_digest:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid(
            "site policy digest does not match the site policy"
        )
    if payload[CP_MOMENT] > verify_moment:
        raise _acf_proof_invalid(
            "moment must not be later than the verification moment"
        )

    key_entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, payload[VD_ISSUER], payload[KEY_VERSION],
        verify_moment,
    )
    expected_signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(key_entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_signature, signature):
        raise AuthenticationError(
            "aggregate chain fork proof signature does not match"
        )

    return {
        FORK_PROOF_CHAINS: copy.deepcopy(chains),
        VD_ISSUER: payload[VD_ISSUER],
        KEY_VERSION: payload[KEY_VERSION],
        CP_MOMENT: payload[CP_MOMENT],
        PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST: expected_prune_digest,
        PAFD_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: expected_site_digest,
        FORK_PROOF_DIGEST: hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
        FORK_PROOF_REPORT: copy.deepcopy(payload[FORK_PROOF_REPORT]),
        VERSION: AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_PROOF_VERSION,
    }


# -- Offline batch verification of aggregate chain fork proofs ----------------

def _acf_proofs_item_report(
    item_id: str, status: str, error: str | None, result: dict | None
) -> dict:
    """One aggregate chain fork proof batch report, fixed key order."""
    return {
        CHECKPOINT_ITEM_ERROR: error,
        ID: item_id,
        VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT: result,
        STATUS: status,
    }


def _verify_acf_fork_proof_item(
    item: dict,
    validated_prune_policy: dict,
    validated_authorization_policy: dict,
    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify one aggregate chain fork proof in isolation.

    Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials and a wrong
    signature make the item ``unauthenticated``; every encoding,
    key-set, version, digest, ordering, reference or report-binding
    fault makes it ``invalid-proof``; a passing proof is ``verified``.
    """
    item_id = item[ID]
    try:
        result = _verify_acf_fork_proof_core(
            item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF],
            validated_prune_policy,
            validated_authorization_policy,
            validated_keyring,
            moment,
        )
    except AuthenticationError as exc:
        return _acf_proofs_item_report(
            item_id, _ACF_PROOFS_UNAUTHENTICATED, str(exc), None
        )
    except (InvalidChainProofError, TypeError) as exc:
        # A TypeError here can only come from a wrong JSON field type
        # *inside* the proof bytes; the public argument types were all
        # validated before the batch ran.
        return _acf_proofs_item_report(
            item_id, _ACF_PROOFS_INVALID, str(exc), None
        )
    return _acf_proofs_item_report(
        item_id, _ACF_PROOFS_VERIFIED, None, result
    )


def verify_aggregate_chain_fork_proofs(items, prune_policy, authorization_policy,
                                      keyring, moment):
    """Verify a whole batch of aggregate chain fork proofs offline.

    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item is a dict with exactly the
    keys ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the batch) and ``proof``
    (the bytes :func:`sign_aggregate_chain_fork_proof` produced).  The
    whole batch structure and the shared prune policy, site
    authorization policy, keyring and moment are validated in full
    before any proof is verified: container, element or field type
    faults raise :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an
    int) and an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong item key
    set raises :class:`ValueError` (the shared materials keep their
    single-entry classification).  Only these batch-level faults raise.

    Each proof is then verified independently, in strict input order,
    through the aggregate chain fork proof rules: one proof's failure
    never stops a later proof or alters an earlier report, and a failed
    item always keeps a null result and a definite non-empty error.
    Unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong
    signature make the item ``unauthenticated``; an illegal encoding,
    key set, version, digest, count, ordering, reference or report
    binding makes it ``invalid-proof``; a passing proof is ``verified``.

    The top-level result is a fresh dict with the fixed keys ``items``
    and ``version`` (the integer 1); each item report carries, in this
    key order, ``error`` (null exactly when verified), ``id``,
    ``result`` (a fresh independent copy of the single-proof result
    when verified, otherwise null -- the identity of an unauthenticated
    payload never enters a result) and ``status``.  Repeated calls
    return equal but mutually independent results.  No file is read or
    written and no input is modified.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_pac_fork_proof_items(items)
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_authorization_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        authorization_policy
    )
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
    return {
        ITEMS: [
            _verify_acf_fork_proof_item(
                item, validated_prune_policy, validated_authorization_policy,
                validated_keyring, verify_moment,
            )
            for item in validated_items
        ],
        VERSION: _ACF_PROOFS_VERSION,
    }


# -- Multi-site threshold adjudication over aggregate chain fork proofs --------

def _adjudicate_acf_one(
    item: dict,
    prune_policy_digest: str,
    site_policy_digest: str,
    authorization_policy: dict,
    keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify, authorize and authenticate one aggregate chain fork proof.

    The proof is first checked through the exact aggregate chain fork
    proof structural rules, then the signing site and key version are
    authorized exactly against the site authorization policy with no
    fallback, and finally the HMAC is checked against the current
    keyring.  Any failure rejects just this row with one fixed reason
    and never affects the other items.
    """
    item_id = item[ID]
    raw_proof = item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF]
    proof_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw_proof).hexdigest()

    def structural_invalid() -> dict:
        return _cf_row(
            item_id, proof_digest, None, None, None,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID, _PAFD_REASON_INVALID_PROOF,
        )

    try:
        payload, signature, _chains = _parse_acf_fork_proof(raw_proof)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return structural_invalid()

    site = payload[VD_ISSUER]
    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
    try:
        edges = _pac_fork_proof_edges(payload)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return structural_invalid()

    def reject(reason: str) -> dict:
        return _cf_row(
            item_id, proof_digest, site, key_version, edges,
            _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID, reason,
        )

    # Both shared policy digests must match and the proof must not be
    # dated after the adjudication moment; a mismatch makes the claimed
    # identity untrustworthy, so the row carries none.  Authorization
    # itself is governed by the separate authorization policy.
    if payload[CF_PROOF_PRUNE_POLICY] != prune_policy_digest:
        return structural_invalid()
    if payload[CF_PROOF_SITE_POLICY] != site_policy_digest:
        return structural_invalid()
    if payload[CP_MOMENT] > moment:
        return structural_invalid()

    allowed_versions = authorization_policy[ADJ_SITES].get(site)
    if allowed_versions is None:
        return reject(REASON_UNAUTHORIZED_SITE)
    if key_version not in allowed_versions:
        return reject(REASON_UNAUTHORIZED_VERSION)

    key_entry = None
    for candidate in keyring.get(site, ()):
        if candidate[VERSION] == key_version:
            key_entry = candidate
            break
    if key_entry is None:
        return reject(REASON_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE)
    if key_entry[REVOKED]:
        return reject(REASON_REVOKED)
    if moment < key_entry[NOT_BEFORE]:
        return reject(REASON_NOT_YET_VALID)
    if moment > key_entry[NOT_AFTER]:
        return reject(REASON_EXPIRED)

    expected_signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(key_entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_signature, signature):
        return reject(REASON_BAD_SIGNATURE)

    return _cf_row(
        item_id, proof_digest, site, key_version, edges,
        _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID, None,
    )


def adjudicate_aggregate_chain_forks(items, prune_policy, authorization_policy,
                                     keyring, moment, issuer, version):
    """Adjudicate multi-site aggregate chain fork proofs offline.

    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a unique
    non-empty ``id`` and ``proof`` bytes produced by
    :func:`sign_aggregate_chain_fork_proof`.  ``prune_policy`` is the
    shared invariant original ``{"batch","sites","threshold"}`` pruning
    policy the proofs were issued against and ``authorization_policy``
    the site authorization policy their payloads digest; it carries
    exactly ``sites`` (a non-empty map of each authorized non-empty
    signing site to its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions)
    and ``threshold`` (a positive integer no greater than the site
    count).  ``keyring`` follows the existing rules, ``moment`` is the
    non-negative adjudication moment and ``issuer``/``version`` name the
    adjudicator credentials.  No file is read or written and no input is
    modified.

    Every proof is first independently re-verified through the
    aggregate chain fork proof rules -- the bound chain summary, fork
    edges, crossing chains and complete batch report are each
    recomputed from the bound materials (a structurally illegal,
    foreign-policy or future-dated proof is ``invalid-proof`` carrying
    no identity) -- then authorized precisely by the exact payload
    identity and key version against the authorization policy with no
    fallback (``unauthorized-site``, ``unauthorized-version``), then
    authenticated against the current keyring
    (``credential-unavailable``, ``revoked``, ``not-yet-valid``,
    ``expired``, ``bad-signature``); one item's rejection never blocks a
    later item.  For one site, proofs whose complete fork edge set --
    every edge of root digest, forking predecessor digest and the
    ascending set of legal successor digests -- is identical count once
    and every extra proof is ``duplicate``, while two distinct complete
    edge sets from one site are a ``contradiction``.  Distinct sites
    must agree exactly on the complete edge set; any same-site
    contradiction or cross-site difference is ``conflicted`` with a null
    common set and can never be outvoted by a majority.  A unique edge
    set backed by at least the threshold of distinct sites is
    ``accepted``; the same unique set short of the threshold is
    ``insufficient`` yet still binds that common set; with no valid vote
    at all the common set is null.

    The packet is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with
    recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte,
    carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``; the payload binds
    exactly the two policy digests -- ``prunePolicyDigest`` and
    ``authorizationPolicyDigest`` -- together with ``common`` (the
    stable-sorted common fork edge set, or null), ``issuer``, ``items``
    (the rows stably sorted by site then id, each carrying
    ``conclusion``, the authenticated ``edges`` or null, ``id``,
    ``issuer``, ``keyVersion``, the proof ``digest`` and ``reason``),
    ``keyVersion``, ``proofs`` (each input proof's SHA-256 in the
    original input order), ``status`` and ``version`` (the integer 1).
    The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical
    payload bytes under the exact adjudicator issuer/version key.

    A parameter, container or public-field type fault raises
    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); an empty
    list, an empty or duplicate id, or an illegal policy, threshold,
    moment, issuer or version raises :class:`ValueError`; unknown,
    revoked, not-yet-valid or expired adjudicator credentials raise
    :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_pac_fork_proof_items(items)
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_authorization_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        authorization_policy
    )
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    if isinstance(moment, bool) or not isinstance(moment, int):
        raise TypeError("moment must be an int")
    if moment < 0:
        raise ValueError("moment must be non-negative")
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise ValueError("issuer must be non-empty")
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
        raise TypeError("version must be an int")
    if version <= 0:
        raise ValueError("version must be positive")

    prune_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _verdict_policy_bytes(validated_prune_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    site_policy_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_authorization_policy)
    ).hexdigest()

    # The proof summaries keep the original input order, independent of
    # the stably sorted conclusion rows.
    proof_digests = [
        hashlib.sha256(item[FORK_PROOF_ITEM_PROOF]).hexdigest()
        for item in validated_items
    ]
    rows = [
        _adjudicate_acf_one(
            item, prune_policy_digest, site_policy_digest,
            validated_authorization_policy, validated_keyring, moment,
        )
        for item in validated_items
    ]

    contradicted, votes = _tally_pac_fork_rows(rows)

    edge_sets = set(votes.values())
    if contradicted or len(edge_sets) > 1:
        status = _CF_STATUS_CONFLICTED
        common = None
    elif len(edge_sets) == 1:
        common = _sorted_pac_fork_edge_objects(next(iter(edge_sets)))
        if len(votes) >= validated_authorization_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD]:
            status = _CF_STATUS_ACCEPTED
        else:
            status = _CF_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
    else:
        status = _CF_STATUS_INSUFFICIENT
        common = None

    rows.sort(
        key=lambda row: (
            row[VD_ISSUER] is not None,
            row[VD_ISSUER] or "",
            row[ID],
        )
    )

    signing_entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, issuer, version, moment
    )
    payload = {
        _CF_DECISION_COMMON: common,
        VD_ISSUER: issuer,
        ITEMS: [copy.deepcopy(row) for row in rows],
        KEY_VERSION: version,
        PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST: prune_policy_digest,
        _CF_DECISION_PROOFS: proof_digests,
        _ACF_AUTHZ_POLICY_DIGEST: hashlib.sha256(
            _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_authorization_policy)
        ).hexdigest(),
        STATUS: status,
        VERSION: AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_VERSION,
    }
    signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(signing_entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return _prune_compact({TICKET_PAYLOAD: payload, SIGNATURE: signature})


def _parse_acf_decision(raw: object) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    """Validate aggregate chain fork decision bytes structurally.

    A non-bytes argument or a field of the wrong type raises
    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); every
    encoding, key-set, version, digest or value-format fault raises
    :class:`InvalidChainDecisionError`.  The policy, tally and
    credential bindings are checked by the decision verifier.
    """
    if not isinstance(raw, bytes):
        raise TypeError("decision must be bytes")
    if not raw or raw[-1:] in (b"\n", b"\r", b" ", b"\t"):
        raise _acf_decision_invalid(
            "must end with the closing brace, no trailing byte"
        )
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid("is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        data = json.loads(
            text,
            object_pairs_hook=_reject_duplicate_acf_decision_keys,
        )
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid("is not valid JSON") from exc

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise TypeError("decision must be a JSON object")
    if set(data.keys()) != _PAFD_DECISION_TOP_KEYS:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid(
            "must contain exactly the keys 'payload' and 'signature'"
        )
    signature = data[SIGNATURE]
    if not isinstance(signature, str):
        raise TypeError("decision signature must be a str")
    if not _prune_is_digest(signature):
        raise _acf_decision_invalid(
            "signature must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
        )
    payload = data[TICKET_PAYLOAD]
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise TypeError("decision payload must be an object")
    if set(payload.keys()) != _ACF_DECISION_PAYLOAD_KEYS:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid(
            "payload must contain exactly the keys 'common', 'issuer', "
            "'items', 'keyVersion', 'prunePolicyDigest', 'proofs', "
            "'authorizationPolicyDigest', 'status' and 'version'"
        )

    issuer = payload[VD_ISSUER]
    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
        raise TypeError("payload issuer must be a str")
    if issuer == "":
        raise _acf_decision_invalid("payload issuer must be a non-empty str")
    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
    if isinstance(key_version, bool) or not isinstance(key_version, int):
        raise TypeError("payload keyVersion must be an int")
    if key_version <= 0:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid("payload keyVersion must be positive")
    status = payload[STATUS]
    if not isinstance(status, str):
        raise TypeError("payload status must be a str")
    if status not in _PAFD_STATUSES:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid("payload status is not a known status")
    for field in (PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST, _ACF_AUTHZ_POLICY_DIGEST):
        digest = payload[field]
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"payload {field} must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                f"payload {field} must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )

    proofs = payload[PAFD_PROOFS]
    if not isinstance(proofs, list):
        raise TypeError("payload proofs must be a list")
    if not proofs:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid("payload proofs must be non-empty")
    for position, digest in enumerate(proofs):
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"payload proof {position} digest must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                f"payload proof {position} digest must be 64 lowercase hex "
                "characters"
            )

    raw_rows = payload[ITEMS]
    if not isinstance(raw_rows, list):
        raise TypeError("payload items must be a list")
    if not raw_rows:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid("payload items must be non-empty")
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    for position, row in enumerate(raw_rows):
        where = f"payload item {position}"
        if not isinstance(row, dict):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} must be an object")
        if set(row.keys()) != _PAFD_ROW_KEYS:
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'conclusion', "
                "'edges', 'id', 'keyVersion', 'digest', 'reason' and "
                "'site'"
            )
        row_id = row[ID]
        if not isinstance(row_id, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} id must be a str")
        if row_id == "":
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(f"{where} id must be non-empty")
        if row_id in seen_ids:
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(f"{where} repeats an id")
        seen_ids.add(row_id)
        digest = row[_CF_PROOF_DIGEST]
        if not isinstance(digest, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} digest must be a str")
        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                f"{where} digest must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )
        site = row[VD_ISSUER]
        if site is not None:
            if not isinstance(site, str):
                raise TypeError(f"{where} site must be a str or null")
            if site == "":
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(f"{where} site must be non-empty")
        row_key_version = row[KEY_VERSION]
        if isinstance(row_key_version, bool) or not isinstance(
            row_key_version, int
        ):
            if row_key_version is not None:
                raise TypeError(f"{where} keyVersion must be an int or null")
        elif row_key_version <= 0:
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(f"{where} keyVersion must be positive")
        if (site is None) != (row_key_version is None):
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                f"{where} site and keyVersion must be null together"
            )
        conclusion = row[ADJ_CONCLUSION]
        if not isinstance(conclusion, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} conclusion must be a str")
        if conclusion not in _PAFD_CONCLUSIONS:
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(f"{where} conclusion is not known")
        reason = row[ADJ_REASON]
        if conclusion == _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID:
            if reason is not None:
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                    f"{where} reason must be null for a valid item"
                )
        else:
            if not isinstance(reason, str):
                raise TypeError(f"{where} reason must be a str")
            if reason not in _PAFD_REASONS:
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(f"{where} reason is not known")
        if conclusion == _PAFD_CONCLUSION_INVALID:
            if reason not in _PAFD_INVALID_REASONS:
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                    f"{where} reason does not match an invalid item"
                )
        elif conclusion != _PAFD_CONCLUSION_VALID:
            if reason != conclusion:
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                    f"{where} reason must match its conclusion"
                )

        raw_edges = row[PAFD_EDGES]
        if raw_edges is not None:
            if not isinstance(raw_edges, list):
                raise TypeError(f"{where} edges must be a list or null")
            if not raw_edges:
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                    f"{where} edges must be non-empty for an authenticated "
                    "proof"
                )
            row_edges = [
                _validated_pafd_edge(value, where, _acf_decision_invalid)
                for value in raw_edges
            ]
            triples = _pac_fork_edge_triples(row_edges)
            if len(set(triples)) != len(triples):
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(f"{where} edges must be unique")
            if list(triples) != sorted(triples):
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                    f"{where} edges must be sorted ascending"
                )
        identity_expected = reason != _PAFD_REASON_INVALID_PROOF
        if identity_expected:
            if site is None or raw_edges is None:
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                    f"{where} an authenticated proof must carry its site and "
                    "fork edges"
                )
        else:
            if site is not None or raw_edges is not None:
                raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                    f"{where} an invalid-proof item must carry no site or "
                    "fork edges"
                )

    common = payload[PAFD_COMMON]
    if common is not None:
        if not isinstance(common, list):
            raise TypeError("payload common must be a list or null")
        if not common:
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                "a bound common edge set must be non-empty"
            )
        common_edges = [
            _validated_pafd_edge(value, "payload common",
                                 _acf_decision_invalid)
            for value in common
        ]
        common_triples = _pac_fork_edge_triples(common_edges)
        if len(set(common_triples)) != len(common_triples) or list(
            common_triples
        ) != sorted(common_triples):
            raise _acf_decision_invalid(
                "payload common edges must be unique and sorted ascending"
            )

    decision_version = payload[VERSION]
    if isinstance(decision_version, bool) or not isinstance(
        decision_version, int
    ):
        raise TypeError("payload version must be an int")
    if decision_version != AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_VERSION:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid("payload version must be the integer 1")

    if _prune_compact(data) != raw:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid(
            "encoding is not the canonical compact form"
        )
    return payload, signature


def verify_aggregate_chain_fork_decision(decision, prune_policy,
                                        authorization_policy, keyring, moment):
    """Re-verify a signed aggregate chain fork decision entirely offline.

    Only the decision bytes, the expected shared ``prune_policy``, the
    expected site ``authorization_policy``, the current ``keyring`` and
    the verification ``moment`` are consulted -- no file is read or
    written and no argument is modified.  The decision binds the two
    policy digests (the prune policy and the site authorization
    policy); the proof site policy is already digested inside every
    signed proof the decision rows name.  Verification validates the
    canonical encoding and every key set, recomputes both policy
    digests, re-tallies the bound per-proof rows purely from the signed
    payload (the stable site/id row ordering, the original-order proof
    digest vector as a multiset independent of the row order, the
    same-site duplicate/contradiction markings, the cross-site complete
    edge-set agreement, the authorization threshold outcome and the
    claimed common set), and checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the
    current keyring binds to the payload's exact issuer and version,
    usable at the verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry
    rejects the decision with no fallback.

    On success a fresh depth-independent mapping is returned with the
    fixed keys ``common``, ``proofDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the decision
    bytes), ``issuer``, ``items``, ``keyVersion``,
    ``prunePolicyDigest``, ``proofs``, ``authorizationPolicyDigest``,
    ``status`` and ``version`` (the integer 1); repeated calls return
    equal but mutually independent objects.  A non-bytes decision or a
    wrong public field type raises :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool`
    never poses as an int); an empty value, a duplicate id, a wrong key
    set or an illegal policy, threshold, moment, site or version raises
    :class:`ValueError`; an illegal decision structure, ordering, tally
    or binding raises :class:`InvalidChainDecisionError` (a
    :class:`ValueError` subclass, distinct from
    :class:`InvalidChainProofError`); unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or
    expired credentials or a wrong signature raise
    :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(decision, bytes):
        raise TypeError("decision must be bytes")
    validated_prune_policy = _validated_adjudication_policy(prune_policy)
    validated_authorization_policy = _validated_prune_batch_site_policy(
        authorization_policy
    )
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")

    payload, signature = _parse_acf_decision(decision)
    expected_prune_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _verdict_policy_bytes(validated_prune_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    if payload[PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST] != expected_prune_digest:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid(
            "prune policy digest does not match the prune policy"
        )
    expected_authorization_digest = hashlib.sha256(
        _prune_batch_site_policy_bytes(validated_authorization_policy)
    ).hexdigest()
    if payload[_ACF_AUTHZ_POLICY_DIGEST] != expected_authorization_digest:
        raise _acf_decision_invalid(
            "authorization policy digest does not match the authorization "
            "policy"
        )

    # The proof digest vector stays in the original input order, so only
    # its multiset must agree with the stably sorted rows.
    status = _reconcile_pafd(
        payload, validated_authorization_policy[ADJ_THRESHOLD],
        invalid=_acf_decision_invalid, positional_proofs=False,
    )

    entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, payload[VD_ISSUER], payload[KEY_VERSION],
        verify_moment,
    )
    expected_signature = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(entry[SECRET]),
        _prune_compact(payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_signature, signature):
        raise AuthenticationError(
            "aggregate chain fork decision signature does not match"
        )

    return {
        key: copy.deepcopy(value)
        for key, value in (
            (PAFD_COMMON, payload[PAFD_COMMON]),
            (FORK_PROOF_DIGEST, hashlib.sha256(decision).hexdigest()),
            (VD_ISSUER, payload[VD_ISSUER]),
            (ITEMS, payload[ITEMS]),
            (KEY_VERSION, payload[KEY_VERSION]),
            (PAFD_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST, expected_prune_digest),
            (PAFD_PROOFS, payload[PAFD_PROOFS]),
            (_ACF_AUTHZ_POLICY_DIGEST, expected_authorization_digest),
            (STATUS, status),
            (VERSION, AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_VERSION),
        )
    }

"""Tests for signed chain fork proofs and their cross-site adjudication.

Covers :func:`sign_chain_fork_proof`, :func:`verify_chain_fork_proof`,
:func:`verify_chain_fork_proofs`, :func:`adjudicate_chain_forks` and
:func:`verify_chain_fork_decision`: the signed proof binding both
shared policy digests, the original-order chain materials (id, root,
every successor and the complete versioned policy history), the
complete fork-chain batch report and the signing moment; offline
re-verification recomputing the chain material digests, fork edges,
crossing chains, conflicted set and report status from the bound
materials alone; the verified/invalid-proof/unauthenticated batch
taxonomy with input-order reports; the verify-then-authorize-then-
authenticate per-proof pipeline with fixed reasons; same-site
duplicate/contradiction handling over the complete fork edge set;
cross-site edge-set agreement and threshold acceptance with the common
set kept on insufficient tallies; the canonical signed decision and
its offline re-tally verification; the distinct
InvalidChainProofError/InvalidChainDecisionError hierarchies;
equal-but-independent results, input immutability and the purely
offline guarantee.
"""

import copy
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import os
import sys
import unittest
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

from offline_coordination.replication import (
    AuthenticationError,
    InvalidChainDecisionError,
    InvalidChainProofError,
    InvalidForkAggregateChainError,
    adjudicate_chain_forks,
    sign_chain_fork_proof,
    verify_chain_fork_decision,
    verify_chain_fork_proof,
    verify_chain_fork_proofs,
)

from test_adjudicate_prune_aggregate_forks import proof_item, site_policy
from test_aggregate_prune_fork_decisions import decision_item
from test_fork_convergence import SECRET_COORD, compact, entry, parse
from test_prune_attestations import JUDGE, SITE_A, SITE_B, SITE_C
from test_supersede_fork_aggregate import ForkAggregateChainFixtures, rewrap

BATCH_REPORT_KEYS = ["items", "version"]
ITEM_REPORT_KEYS = ["error", "id", "result", "status"]
PROOF_KEYS = ["payload", "signature"]
PROOF_PAYLOAD_KEYS = [
    "chains", "issuer", "keyVersion", "moment", "prunePolicy", "report",
    "sitePolicy", "version",
]
PROOF_CHAIN_KEYS = ["id", "policies", "root", "successors"]
PROOF_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "chains", "issuer", "keyVersion", "moment", "prunePolicyDigest",
    "sitePolicyDigest", "proofDigest", "report", "version",
]
DECISION_PAYLOAD_KEYS = [
    "common", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion", "proofs",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "sitePolicyDigest", "status", "version",
]
ROW_KEYS = ["conclusion", "digest", "edges", "id", "issuer",
            "keyVersion", "reason"]
EDGE_KEYS = ["predecessorDigest", "rootDigest", "successors"]
DECISION_RESULT_KEYS = [
    "common", "proofDigest", "issuer", "items", "keyVersion",
    "prunePolicyDigest", "proofs", "sitePolicyDigest", "status", "version",
]


class ChainForkFixtures(ForkAggregateChainFixtures):
    """Forking fork-aggregate chain batches and chain fork proof helpers."""

    def setUp(self):  # noqa: D102
        super().setUp()
        self.m = self.moment + 20
        self.sp = self.sp
        self.first_a = self.fsucc(
            self.root_one, [decision_item("two", self.decision_b)])
        # A genuinely different first successor: a pure policy rotation.
        self.first_b = self.fsucc(
            self.root_one, [], old=self.pv1, new=self.pv2_t1)
        # A third distinct first successor carrying a different decision.
        self.first_c = self.fsucc(
            self.root_one,
            [decision_item("three", self.decision_sa)],
            old=self.pv1, new=self.pv1,
            moment=self.m, effective=self.moment,
        )
        self.cf_items_one = [
            self.fcitem("b", self.root_one, [self.first_b],
                        policies=[self.pv1, self.pv2_t1]),
            self.fcitem("a", self.root_one, [self.first_a]),
        ]
        self.cf_items_two = [
            self.fcitem("b", self.root_one, [self.first_c]),
            self.fcitem("a", self.root_one, [self.first_a]),
        ]

    def csign_proof(self, items=None, issuer=SITE_A, moment=None, version=1,
                   prune_policy=None, site_policy_=None, ring=None):
        return sign_chain_fork_proof(
            self.cf_items_one if items is None else items,
            self.policy if prune_policy is None else prune_policy,
            self.sp if site_policy_ is None else site_policy_,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment, issuer, version,
        )

    def cproof(self, items=None, issuer=SITE_A, moment=None):
        return self.csign_proof(items=items, issuer=issuer, moment=moment)

    def vproof(self, raw, moment=None, prune_policy=None,
               site_policy_=None, ring=None):
        return verify_chain_fork_proof(
            raw,
            self.policy if prune_policy is None else prune_policy,
            self.sp if site_policy_ is None else site_policy_,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment,
        )

    def proofs_report(self, items, **kwargs):
        return verify_chain_fork_proofs(
            items, self.policy, self.sp, self.ring, self.m, **kwargs)

    def make_decision(self, items, sp=None, ring=None, moment=None,
                      issuer=JUDGE, version=1):
        return adjudicate_chain_forks(
            items, self.policy, self.sp if sp is None else sp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment, issuer, version,
        )

    def verify_decision(self, raw, sp=None, ring=None, moment=None):
        return verify_chain_fork_decision(
            raw, self.policy, self.sp if sp is None else sp,
            self.ring if ring is None else ring,
            self.m if moment is None else moment,
        )

    def tamper_proof(self, proof, mutate):
        """Mutate the payload and re-sign with the same signer secret."""
        data = parse(proof)
        mutate(data["payload"])
        data["signature"] = hmac.new(
            bytes.fromhex(SECRET_COORD), compact(data["payload"]),
            hashlib.sha256,
        ).hexdigest()
        return compact(data)


class ProofSignTest(ChainForkFixtures):
    def test_canonical_compact_encoding_without_trailing_byte(self):
        raw = self.cproof()
        self.assertIsInstance(raw, bytes)
        self.assertTrue(raw.endswith(b"}"))
        self.assertNotIn(b"\n", raw)
        self.assertEqual(compact(parse(raw)), raw)
        data = parse(raw)
        self.assertEqual(list(data.keys()), PROOF_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(list(data["payload"].keys()), PROOF_PAYLOAD_KEYS)

    def test_identity_moment_and_version_bindings(self):
        payload = parse(self.cproof())["payload"]
        self.assertEqual(payload["issuer"], SITE_A)
        self.assertEqual(payload["keyVersion"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(payload["moment"], self.m)
        self.assertEqual(payload["version"], 1)
        self.assertNotIsInstance(payload["version"], bool)

    def test_chains_bind_every_material_digest_in_input_order(self):
        payload = parse(self.cproof())["payload"]
        chains = payload["chains"]
        self.assertEqual([chain["id"] for chain in chains], ["b", "a"])
        self.assertEqual(chains[0]["root"],
                         hashlib.sha256(self.root_one).hexdigest())
        self.assertEqual(chains[0]["successors"],
                         [hashlib.sha256(self.first_b).hexdigest()])
        self.assertEqual(chains[1]["successors"],
                         [hashlib.sha256(self.first_a).hexdigest()])
        for chain in chains:
            self.assertEqual(list(chain.keys()), PROOF_CHAIN_KEYS)
        # The complete versioned policy history is bound per stage.
        self.assertEqual(
            chains[0]["policies"],
            [hashlib.sha256(compact({
                "policyVersion": pol["policyVersion"],
                "sites": {site: sorted(pol["sites"][site])
                          for site in sorted(pol["sites"])},
                "threshold": pol["threshold"],
            })).hexdigest()
             for pol in (self.pv1, self.pv2_t1)],
        )
        self.assertEqual(chains[1]["policies"],
                         [hashlib.sha256(compact({
                             "policyVersion": self.pv1["policyVersion"],
                             "sites": {
                                 site: sorted(self.pv1["sites"][site])
                                 for site in sorted(self.pv1["sites"])},
                             "threshold": self.pv1["threshold"],
                         })).hexdigest()] * 2)

    def test_both_policy_digests_are_bound(self):
        payload = parse(self.cproof())["payload"]
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["prunePolicy"],
            hashlib.sha256(compact({
                "batch": self.policy["batch"],
                "sites": {
                    site: sorted(self.policy["sites"][site])
                    for site in sorted(self.policy["sites"])
                },
                "threshold": self.policy["threshold"],
            })).hexdigest(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["sitePolicy"],
            hashlib.sha256(compact({
                "sites": {
                    site: sorted(self.sp["sites"][site])
                    for site in sorted(self.sp["sites"])
                },
                "threshold": self.sp["threshold"],
            })).hexdigest(),
        )

    def test_the_complete_report_is_bound(self):
        raw = self.cproof()
        from offline_coordination.replication import verify_fork_aggregate_chains
        self.assertEqual(
            parse(raw)["payload"]["report"],
            verify_fork_aggregate_chains(
                self.cf_items_one, self.policy, self.sp, self.ring, self.m),
        )

    def test_a_fork_free_batch_is_a_value_error(self):
        no_fork = [self.fcitem("x", self.root_one, [self.first_a])]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.csign_proof(no_fork)

    def test_sign_argument_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.csign_proof([])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one + self.cf_items_one)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one, issuer=9)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one, issuer="")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one, version=True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one, version=0)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one, moment=True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one, moment=-1)

    def test_sign_credential_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one, issuer="ghost")
        revoked = dict(self.ring)
        revoked[SITE_A] = revoked[SITE_A] + [
            entry(2, "22" * 32, revoked=True)]
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.csign_proof(self.cf_items_one, ring=revoked, version=2)

    def test_shared_policy_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.csign_proof(
                self.cf_items_one,
                prune_policy={"batch": "x"},
            )
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.csign_proof(
                self.cf_items_one,
                site_policy_=site_policy(sites=(SITE_A,), threshold=2),
            )


class ProofVerifyTest(ChainForkFixtures):
    def setUp(self):  # noqa: D102
        super().setUp()
        self.raw = self.cproof()

    def test_result_shape_and_bindings(self):
        result = self.vproof(self.raw)
        self.assertEqual(list(result.keys()), PROOF_RESULT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(result["version"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["issuer"], SITE_A)
        self.assertEqual(result["keyVersion"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["moment"], self.m)
        self.assertEqual(result["proofDigest"],
                         hashlib.sha256(self.raw).hexdigest())
        payload = parse(self.raw)["payload"]
        self.assertEqual(result["prunePolicyDigest"], payload["prunePolicy"])
        self.assertEqual(result["sitePolicyDigest"], payload["sitePolicy"])
        self.assertEqual(result["report"], payload["report"])
        self.assertEqual(result["chains"], payload["chains"])

    def test_results_are_equal_but_independent(self):
        first = self.vproof(self.raw)
        second = self.vproof(self.raw)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first["report"], second["report"])
        first["report"]["items"][0]["status"] = "verified"
        first["chains"][0]["root"] = "00" * 32
        again = self.vproof(self.raw)
        self.assertEqual(again["report"]["items"][0]["status"], "conflicted")
        self.assertNotEqual(again["chains"][0]["root"], "00" * 32)

    def test_public_argument_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.vproof("not-bytes")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, prune_policy="not-a-dict")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, site_policy_="not-a-dict")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.vproof(self.raw,
                        prune_policy={"batch": "b", "sites": {}, "threshold": 1})
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, moment=True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, moment=-1)

    def test_wrong_prune_policy_is_a_proof_error(self):
        other = {"batch": "other",
                 "sites": {site: {1} for site in self.policy["sites"]},
                 "threshold": self.policy["threshold"]}
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, prune_policy=other)

    def test_wrong_site_policy_is_a_proof_error(self):
        other = site_policy(
            sites=tuple(self.sp["sites"]),
            threshold=1,
        )
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, site_policy_=other)

    def test_verification_before_signing_moment_is_a_proof_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, moment=self.m - 1)

    def test_encoding_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.raw + b"\n")
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(b"not-json")
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(json.dumps(parse(self.raw), indent=2).encode())
        duplicated = self.raw.decode("utf-8").replace(
            '"version":1', '"version":1,"version":1', 1).encode()
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(duplicated)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.vproof(b"[]")
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(b"")

    def test_payload_field_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p.__setitem__("version", 2)))
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p.__setitem__("version", True)))
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p.__setitem__("issuer", "")))
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p.__setitem__("keyVersion", 0)))
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p.__setitem__("prunePolicy", "00" * 32)))
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p.__setitem__("sitePolicy", "00" * 32)))

    def test_chain_material_binding_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p["chains"].pop(0)))
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p["chains"].reverse()))

        def swap_successor(payload):
            payload["chains"][0]["successors"][0] = "00" * 32
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(self.raw, swap_successor))

        def drop_policy(payload):
            payload["chains"][0]["policies"].pop(0)
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(self.raw, drop_policy))

    def test_report_binding_faults(self):
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(
                self.raw, lambda p: p["report"].__setitem__("forks", [])))

        def tamper_ids(payload):
            payload["report"]["forks"][0]["ids"] = ["a"]
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(self.raw, tamper_ids))

        def tamper_successors(payload):
            payload["report"]["forks"][0]["successors"] = ["00" * 32] * 2
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(self.raw, tamper_successors))

        def tamper_status(payload):
            payload["report"]["items"][0]["status"] = "verified"
            payload["report"]["items"][0]["error"] = None
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(self.raw, tamper_status))

        def tamper_error(payload):
            payload["report"]["items"][0]["error"] = "something-else"
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(self.raw, tamper_error))

        def tamper_head(payload):
            payload["report"]["items"][0]["result"]["headDigest"] = "00" * 32
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainProofError):
            self.vproof(self.tamper_proof(self.raw, tamper_head))

    def test_conflicted_report_uses_the_fac_fixed_error(self):
        for item in parse(self.raw)["payload"]["report"]["items"]:
            self.assertEqual(item["error"], "forked-fork-aggregate-chain")

    def test_unknown_revoked_future_expired_credentials_are_authentication(self):
        missing = {site: keys for site, keys in self.ring.items()
                   if site != SITE_A}
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, ring=missing)
        revoked = dict(self.ring)
        revoked[SITE_A] = [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, revoked=True)]
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, ring=revoked)
        future = dict(self.ring)
        future[SITE_A] = [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, not_before=self.m + 1)]
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, ring=future)
        expired = dict(self.ring)
        expired[SITE_A] = [entry(1, SECRET_COORD, not_after=self.m - 1)]
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.vproof(self.raw, ring=expired)

    def test_bad_signature_is_authentication(self):
        data = parse(self.raw)
        data["signature"] = "0" * 64
        with self.assertRaises(AuthenticationError):
            self.vproof(compact(data))

    def test_error_hierarchy(self):
        self.assertTrue(issubclass(InvalidChainProofError, ValueError))
        self.assertTrue(issubclass(InvalidChainDecisionError, ValueError))
        self.assertTrue(issubclass(AuthenticationError, ValueError))
        self.assertIsNot(InvalidChainProofError, InvalidForkAggregateChainError)
        self.assertIsNot(InvalidChainProofError, InvalidChainDecisionError)


class BatchVerifyTest(ChainForkFixtures):
    def test_reports_in_input_order(self):
        p_a = self.cproof(issuer=SITE_A)
        p_b = self.cproof(issuer=SITE_B)
        report = self.proofs_report([
            proof_item("a", p_a), proof_item("b", b"{}"),
            proof_item("c", p_b),
        ])
        self.assertEqual(list(report.keys()), BATCH_REPORT_KEYS)
        self.assertEqual(report["version"], 1)
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in report["items"]],
                         ["a", "b", "c"])
        self.assertEqual([row["status"] for row in report["items"]],
                         ["verified", "invalid-proof", "verified"])
        for row in report["items"]:
            self.assertEqual(list(row.keys()), ITEM_REPORT_KEYS)
        self.assertIsNone(report["items"][0]["error"])
        self.assertEqual(
            report["items"][0]["result"]["proofDigest"],
            hashlib.sha256(p_a).hexdigest(),
        )
        bad = report["items"][1]
        self.assertIsNone(bad["result"])
        self.assertTrue(bad["error"])

    def test_unauthenticated_is_isolated(self):
        ring = {site: [entry(1, "77" * 32)]
                for site in (SITE_A, SITE_B, SITE_C, JUDGE)}
        report = self.proofs_report(
            [proof_item("a", self.cproof(issuer=SITE_A)),
             proof_item("b", self.cproof(issuer=SITE_B))],
        ) if False else verify_chain_fork_proofs(
            [proof_item("a", self.cproof(issuer=SITE_A)),
             proof_item("b", self.cproof(issuer=SITE_B))],
            self.policy, self.sp, ring, self.m,
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            [row["status"] for row in report["items"]],
            ["unauthenticated", "unauthenticated"],
        )
        self.assertTrue(all(row["error"] for row in report["items"]))

    def test_structure_validated_upfront(self):
        p_a = self.cproof()
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.proofs_report("x")
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.proofs_report(["x"])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.proofs_report([])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.proofs_report([proof_item("a", p_a), proof_item("a", p_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.proofs_report([{"id": "a", "proof": p_a, "x": 1}])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.proofs_report([proof_item("", p_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.proofs_report([proof_item(1, p_a)])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.proofs_report([proof_item("a", "x")])

    def test_shared_materials_validated_upfront(self):
        items = [proof_item("a", self.cproof())]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_proofs(items, {"batch": "x"}, self.sp,
                                    self.ring, self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_proofs(items, self.policy,
                                    site_policy(sites=(SITE_A,), threshold=2),
                                    self.ring, self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            verify_chain_fork_proofs(items, self.policy, self.sp,
                                    "ring", self.m)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            verify_chain_fork_proofs(items, self.policy, self.sp,
                                    self.ring, True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            verify_chain_fork_proofs(items, self.policy, self.sp,
                                    self.ring, -1)

    def test_results_are_fresh_and_independent(self):
        items = [proof_item("a", self.cproof())]
        first = self.proofs_report(items)
        second = self.proofs_report(items)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first, second)
        self.assertIsNot(first["items"][0]["result"],
                         second["items"][0]["result"])
        first["items"][0]["result"]["issuer"] = "tampered"
        self.assertEqual(
            self.proofs_report(items)["items"][0]["result"]["issuer"], SITE_A)

            ({k: v for k, v in self.ring.items() if k != SITE_A},
             "credential-unavailable"),
            (self._ring_with(
                SITE_A, entry(1, SECRET_COORD, revoked=True)), "revoked"),
            (self._ring_with(
                SITE_A, entry(1, SECRET_COORD, not_before=self.m + 1)),
             "not-yet-valid"),

                SITE_A, entry(1, SECRET_COORD, not_after=self.m - 1)),
             "expired"),

            rows = self.row_by_id([proof_item("x", p)], ring=modified)

class DecisionPacketShapeTest(ChainForkFixtures):
    def setUp(self):  # noqa: D102
        super().setUp()
        self.p_a = self.cproof(issuer=SITE_A)
        self.p_b = self.cproof(issuer=SITE_B)
        self.items = [proof_item("x", self.p_a), proof_item("y", self.p_b)]
        self.raw = self.make_decision(self.items)

    def test_canonical_compact_without_trailing_byte(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.raw.endswith(b"}"))
        self.assertNotIn(b"\n", self.raw)
        self.assertEqual(compact(parse(self.raw)), self.raw)
        self.assertEqual(list(parse(self.raw).keys()), ["payload", "signature"])
        self.assertEqual(list(parse(self.raw)["payload"].keys()),
                         DECISION_PAYLOAD_KEYS)

    def test_row_shapes_and_proof_digests(self):
        payload = parse(self.raw)["payload"]
        for row in payload["items"]:
            self.assertEqual(list(row.keys()), ROW_KEYS)
            expected = self.p_a if row["id"] == "x" else self.p_b
            self.assertEqual(row["digest"],
                             hashlib.sha256(expected).hexdigest())
            for edge in row["edges"]:
                self.assertEqual(list(edge.keys()), EDGE_KEYS)

    def test_proofs_align_term_by_term_with_the_canonical_rows(self):
        payload = parse(self.raw)["payload"]
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["proofs"],
            [row["digest"] for row in payload["items"]],
        )
        self.assertEqual(payload["proofs"], [
            hashlib.sha256(self.p_a).hexdigest(),
            hashlib.sha256(self.p_b).hexdigest(),
        ])
        # The summary order is the canonical row order, not the raw input
        # order: reversing the inputs leaves the signed proofs vector
        # (and rows) unchanged.
        reversed_raw = self.make_decision(list(reversed(self.items)))
        reversed_payload = parse(reversed_raw)["payload"]
        self.assertEqual(reversed_payload["proofs"], payload["proofs"])
        self.assertEqual(
            [row["id"] for row in reversed_payload["items"]],
            [row["id"] for row in payload["items"]],
        )

    def test_reordered_proofs_cannot_be_resigned(self):
        payload = parse(self.raw)["payload"]
        tampered = dict(payload)
        tampered["proofs"] = list(reversed(payload["proofs"]))
        with self.assertRaises(InvalidChainDecisionError):
            self.verify_decision(rewrap(tampered))

    def test_policy_digest_and_identity_bindings(self):
        payload = parse(self.raw)["payload"]
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["prunePolicyDigest"],
            hashlib.sha256(compact({
                "batch": self.policy["batch"],
                "sites": {
                    site: sorted(self.policy["sites"][site])
                    for site in sorted(self.policy["sites"])
                },
                "threshold": self.policy["threshold"],
            })).hexdigest(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            payload["sitePolicyDigest"],
            hashlib.sha256(compact({
                "sites": {
                    site: sorted(self.sp["sites"][site])
                    for site in sorted(self.sp["sites"])
                },
                "threshold": self.sp["threshold"],
            })).hexdigest(),
        )
        self.assertEqual(payload["issuer"], JUDGE)
        self.assertEqual(payload["keyVersion"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(payload["version"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(payload["status"], "accepted")

90	def rewrap(payload, secret=SECRET_COORD):
91	    """Re-sign an envelope payload into canonical compact packet bytes."""
92	    signature = hmac.new(
93	        bytes.fromhex(secret), compact(payload), hashlib.sha256
94	    ).hexdigest()
95	    return compact({"payload": payload, "signature": signature})
